rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb for stopping sleeping or waking up.

example.english: I wake up at seven every day.
example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 jat6 cat1 dim2 seng2

rows.note: Use this all-purpose expression for the area behind a moving person or object.

example.english: A truck drove past, sending up a cloud of dust in its wake.
example.traditional: 架貨車駛過，佢後面揚起一陣塵。
example.jyutping: gaa3 fo3 ce1 sai2 gwo3 keoi5 hau6 min6 joeng4 hei2 jat1 zan6 can4

rows.note: Use this when someone or something causes another person to wake up.

example.english: The alarm will wake me at seven.
example.jyutping: naau6 zung1 cat1 dim2 giu3 seng2 ngo5

rows.note: Use this for the trail or disturbance of water left by a boat, especially when it is visibly wave-like.

example.english: The speedboat passed, leaving a huge wake.
example.traditional: 艘快艇駛過，船尾浪好大。
example.jyutping: sau1 faai3 ting5 sai2 gwo3 syun4 mei5 long6 hou2 daai6

rows.note: Use this formal technical term for a wake in fluid dynamics, especially an aircraft's turbulent air trail.

example.english: An aircraft's wake can cause a following aircraft to encounter turbulence.
example.traditional: 飛機尾流會令後方航機遇上亂流。
example.jyutping: fei1 gei1 mei5 lau4 wui5 ling6 hau6 fong1 hong4 gei1 jyu6 soeng6 lyun6 lau4

rows.note: Use this when emphasizing that someone remains awake rather than simply waking up.

example.english: Stay awake until I wake up.
example.jyutping: seng2 zyu6 dang2 ngo5 sing2 faan1 aa3

rows.note: Use this for the visible splash or disturbed water made by a person or animal moving through water.

example.english: They swam very fast, sending up lots of splashes in their wake.
example.traditional: 佢游水游得好快，後面濺起好多水花。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jau4 seoi2 jau4 dak1 hou2 faai3 hau6 min6 zin3 hei2 hou2 do1 seoi2 faa1
